"%1$s" is requesting access to NeoDhizuku. Tap to handle it (use this if the dialog did not appear on its own).
Activate as device owner without removing accounts. Requires Android 13 or newer and Shizuku.

During activation, user_setup_complete is temporarily set to 0. While it is 0, the Home and Recents keys of three-button navigation stop working (Back still works; full-screen gesture navigation is unaffected). It is restored automatically when the flow finishes — if it fails midway, be sure to run step 3 (manual restore).
Limits: Android 13 (API 33) or newer only; requires Shizuku or root to run shell commands; some vendor ROMs may block the required interfaces.
This mode relies on the device policy management role introduced in Android 13. The current system version is %1$s. Please activate via Shizuku or ADB instead.
Grants the device policy management role and sets user_setup_complete to 0, opening the gate required for activation.
Syncs state, registers as a device admin, then activates device owner. user_setup_complete is restored automatically afterwards.
Restores user_setup_complete to 1. Run this step if the navigation keys stopped working.
API service switch, whitelist, behavior after the service is closed, device owner transfer
Behavior after the service is closed
Determines how the service responds when third-party apps call in.
The app can find the service; dangerous operations are refused.
The app can find the service; dangerous operations report success but are not carried out.
The app can find and bind the service, but every call fails. No dialog is shown.
The app can find and bind the service; every call reports success but nothing is carried out. No dialog is shown.
Neither refuses nor allows; the request is left hanging and the app waits forever.
API master switch: disabled, third-party apps cannot use it
!Setup wizard not restored, please run manual restore!

Applies only when the current identity cannot perform a requested action (for example, requesting an owner-only operation while only device admin). The attempt is always logged, regardless of the chosen response.
The caller receives an error. Recommended — avoids silent no-ops.
The caller believes it succeeded, but nothing happens. For apps that crash on errors.
No response is sent; the caller waits indefinitely.
Blocked a request from "%1$s" to wipe device data

The DevicePolicyManager method table could not be loaded, so all device policy calls are now being blocked as a precaution. You can turn off the wipe / owner transfer guards in settings to restore normal use.
"%1$s" is requesting to wipe all device data. This erases accounts, apps, photos and files, and cannot be undone.
Are you sure you want to let "%1$s" wipe this device? This is your second and final warning.
This will erase all data on the device. There is no way to recover afterwards.
I understand the consequences and accept them
Once allowed, the caller may retry within 5 minutes. The grant is single-use and then expires.

View which apps hold delegated device-owner capabilities, and grant them to other apps

Delegation lets an ordinary app call a limited set of device-owner operations. It is independent of the authorization switch here, so revoking access in this app does not withdraw capabilities that were already delegated. Apps normally request delegation by themselves; you can also grant it to them here.
Device owner is required to read or change delegation.
